newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil bond fraud probe summons big bankers.
newsitem.headline: Brazil bond fraud probe summons big bankers.

text.p: Congressional investigators of a multi-million-dollar municipal bond fraud scheme have summoned the chiefs of some of Brazil's biggest banks to testify on the racket, officials said on Thursday.

A spokeswoman for the Senate Parliamentary Committee of Inquiry (CPI) said the presidents of federal mortgage bank Caixa Economica Federal, private bank Bradesco, Lloyds TSB Group Plc-owned Banco Multiplic SA and Parana state bank Banestado had been called.
"They will testify on Monday," she said.
The heads of the large parastatal pension funds of Embratel (Telos), Petrobras (Petros), the Caixa Economica (Funcef) and Serpro (Serpros) will testify on Friday, she added.

Market players had previously said they feared the CPI could get out of control if it targeted high-fliers in the banking sector. But there was no nervousness in the markets on Thursday, brokers said.

The Senate probe, which has gripped media attention for weeks, has allegedly found that states and cities sold debt at below market cost to friendly brokerages. Middlemen and officials allegedly shared the profits.
The heads of the banks and pension funds have been asked to explain why their institutions ended up with the debt once it passed through several hands.
According to Globo newspaper, the CPI believed Bradesco had lost 50 million reais buying the securities and other banks lost smaller amounts. No one was immediately available for comment at Bradesco.
The bond investigation has been inching closer to what CPI senators call the "big fish".
Over the weekend, former Sao Paulo mayor and presidential hopeful Paulo Maluf issued vigorous denials that he was in any way involved.
He also defended his chosen successor as Sao Paulo mayor, Celso Pitta, from accusations of wrong-doing.
The CPI has also focused on the Central Bank's role in regulating and supervising bond issues, with senators baying for the blood of the bank's public debt department head, Jairo da Cruz Ferreira.
Ferreira on Monday quietly took a three-month leave of absence from the bank. Officials denied there was any link.

In addition to the illicit profits made through the bond issues, senators say hard-up states and cities illegally used the money raised for day to day running costs and for infrastructure projects. Under the 1988 constitution, the funds should only have been used to pay off court settlements.
At least three governors -- those of Alagoas, Penambuco and Santa Catarina states -- have been fighting off possible impeachment for misuse of funds.
